description:
"Beyond Time, Beyond Stars"

We are developers skilled in full-stack development and engineering. Tackling the "Abandoned but not Forgotten," we are building a website to honor and tell the stories of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.
summary: With Left Behind, we wanted young space fans to discover that the hardware NASA left on the Moon and Mars wasn't simply abandoned. Most of it was left on purpose. Our project addresses the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge as an interactive 3D website. Players become junior space archaeologists: they fly a spaceship from Earth, warp to the Moon or Mars, land at real landing sites, and explore on foot to find the equipment left behind. Each discovery unlocks the real story: what the object was, why the mission left it, and the science it made possible. It turns a list of "space junk" into a story about engineering choices, written for ages 10 to 15 and suited to classrooms, science clubs, and outreach events.
details:
What it does: Left Behind is an interactive 3D website where you play a junior space archaeologist. After a short scrolling intro, you take off from Earth in your spaceship, warp to the Moon or Mars, and land at real landing sites. You explore on foot under each world’s real gravity and find the equipment NASA left behind. Each find unlocks its story: what it is, why it was left, the science it enabled, and where it is now, with a link to the NASA source.

Benefits and impact: It turns “space junk” into a story about engineering choices. A rocket can only carry so much, so every mission had to decide what stayed. Students aged [10 to 15] learn by exploring instead of reading, and it runs in any browser, so classrooms and outreach events can use it.


Tech stack:

  • Vite, React, TypeScript
  • React Three Fiber and drei (3D), Rapier (physics)
  • HTML/CSS overlays; responsive layout
  • Static site, deployed on GitHub Pages and Vercel
